newsitem.title: THAILAND: Cambodia's Prince Ranariddh visits loyalists.
newsitem.headline: Cambodia's Prince Ranariddh visits loyalists.

text.p: Cambodia's ousted co-premier, Prince Norodom Ranariddh, travelled to the Thai-Cambodian border on Saturday to visit his royalist supporters, an official in the prince's party said.
Ranariddh arrived in Thailand earlier on Saturday in the latest stage of a campaign to drum up diplomatic support.
"He's gone up to Surin to see his people," the official in the prince's FUNCINPEC party said. He declined to elaborate.
Surin is a northeastern Thai province bordering an area of Cambodia under the control of the prince's troops.
Ranariddh, toppled by Second Prime Minister Hun Sen in a coup on July 6, arrived earlier at Bangkok's Don Muang airport from France but declined to speak to reporters, Thai television said.

Many royalist officials and supporters fled from Cambodia to Thailand after the prince was toppled and a subsequent crackdown in which some 40 of his supporters were killed, according to U.N. human rights officials.
Since his removal, Ranariddh has vowed to travel the world to drum up support for a non-violent solution to the crisis in Cambodia and to prevent civil war.
The prince's troops were pushed out of Phnom Penh over two days of fighting in early July and have retreated to the remote northwest after clashes since then.
Ranariddh was based on the same stretch of the Thai-Cambodian border in the 1980s, commanding royalist guerrillas fighting Hun Sen's government in Phnom Penh.
Ranariddh and Hun Sen formed a shaky power-sharing coalition after U.N.-supervised elections in 1993.
The prince was expected to stay in Thailand for a few days, the television report said.
